verses.zh: 雅各家，称为以色列名下，从犹大水源出来的，当听我言！你们指着耶和华的名起誓，提说以色列的　神，却不凭诚实，不凭公义。
verses.en: Listen to this, O family of Jacob,[NOTE:1] you who are called by the name “Israel,”and are descended from Judah,[NOTE:2] who take oaths in the name of the Lordand invoke[NOTE:3] the God of Israel—but not in an honest and just manner.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “house of Jacob”; TEV, CEV “people of Israel.”

The Hebrew text reads literally “and from the waters of Judah came out.” מִמֵּי (mimme) could be a variation from an original מִמְּעֵי (mimmeʿe, “from the inner parts of”). The translation above as well as several other translations treat the text this way or understand that this is what the Hebrew phrase figuratively means (cf. HCSB, NASB, NIV, NLT, NRSV). Some translations (ESV, NKJV) retain the MT reading and render it literally as “waters.” The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa, which corrects a similar form to “from inner parts of” in 39:7, does not do it here.
Heb “cause to remember”; KJV, ASV “make mention of.”
Heb “not in truth and not in righteousness.”

verses.zh: 他们自称为圣城的人，所倚靠的是名为万军之耶和华―以色列的　神。
verses.en: Indeed, they live in the holy city;[NOTE:1] they trust in[NOTE:2] the God of Israel,whose name is the Lord of Heaven’s Armies.
notes: Heb “they call themselves [or “are called”] from the holy city.” The precise meaning of the statement is uncertain. The Niphal of קָרָא (qaraʾ) is combined with the preposition מִן (min) only here. When the Qal of קָרָא is used with מִן, the preposition often indicates the place from which one is summoned (see 46:11). So one could translate, “from the holy city they are summoned,” meaning that they reside there.
Heb “lean on” (so NASB, NRSV); NAB, NIV “rely on.”

verses.zh: 主说：早先的事，我从古时说明，已经出了我的口，也是我所指示的；我忽然行做，事便成就。
verses.en: “I announced events beforehand,[NOTE:1] I issued the decrees and made the predictions;[NOTE:2] suddenly I acted and they came to pass.
notes: Heb “the former things beforehand I declared.”
Heb “and from my mouth they came forth, and I caused them to be heard.”

verses.zh: 因为我素来知道你是顽梗的―你的颈项是铁的；你的额是铜的。
verses.en: I did this[NOTE:1] because I know how stubborn you are.Your neck muscles are like ironand your forehead like bronze.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “I did this” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. In the Hebrew text v. 4 is subordinated to v. 3.
The image is that of a person who has tensed the muscles of the face and neck as a sign of resolute refusal.

verses.zh: 所以，我从古时将这事给你说明，在未成以先指示你，免得你说：这些事是我的偶像所行的，是我雕刻的偶像和我铸造的偶像所命定的。
verses.en: I announced them to you beforehand;before they happened, I predicted them for you,so you could never say,‘My image did these things,my idol, my cast image, decreed them.’

verses.zh: 你已经听见，现在要看见这一切；你不说明吗？从今以后，我将新事，就是你所不知道的隐密事指示你。
verses.en: You have heard; now look at all the evidence![NOTE:1] Will you not admit that what I say is true?[NOTE:2] From this point on I am announcing to you new eventsthat are previously unrevealed and you do not know about.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “gaze [at] all of it”; KJV “see all this.”
Heb “[as for] you, will you not declare?”
Heb “and hidden things, and you do not know them.”

verses.zh: 这事是现今造的，并非从古就有；在今日以先，你也未曾听见，免得你说：这事我早已知道了。
verses.en: Now they come into being,[NOTE:1] not in the past;before today you did not hear about them,so you could not say,‘Yes,[NOTE:2] I know about them.’
notes: Heb “are created” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “They are brand new.”
Heb “look”; KJV, NASB “Behold.”

verses.zh: 你未曾听见，未曾知道；你的耳朵从来未曾开通。我原知道你行事极其诡诈，你自从出胎以来，便称为悖逆的。
verses.en: You did not hear,you do not know,you were not told beforehand.[NOTE:1] For I know that you are very deceitful;[NOTE:2] you were labeled[NOTE:3] a rebel from birth.
notes: Heb “beforehand your ear did not open.”
Heb “deceiving, you deceive.” The infinitive absolute precedes the finite verb for emphasis.
Or “called” (KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 我为我的名暂且忍怒，为我的颂赞向你容忍，不将你剪除。
verses.en: For the sake of my reputation[NOTE:1] I hold back my anger;for the sake of my prestige[NOTE:2] I restrain myself from destroying you.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “for the sake of my name” (so NAB, NASB); NLT “for my own sake.”
Heb “and my praise.” לְמַעַן (lemaʿan, “for the sake of”) is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
Heb “I restrain [myself] concerning you not to cut you off.”

verses.zh: 我熬炼你，却不像熬炼银子；你在苦难的炉中，我拣选你。
verses.en: Look, I have refined you, but not as silver;I have purified you[NOTE:1] in the furnace of misery.
notes: The Hebrew text has בְּחַרְתִּיךָ (bekhartikha, “I have chosen you”), but the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa reads correctly בחנתיכה (“I have tested you”). The metallurgical background of the imagery suggests that purification through testing is the idea.

verses.zh: 我为自己的缘故必行这事，我焉能使我的名被亵渎？我必不将我的荣耀归给假神。
verses.en: For my sake alone[NOTE:1] I will act,for how can I allow my name to be defiled?[NOTE:2] I will not share my glory with anyone else![NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew text repeats לְמַעֲנִי (lemaʿani, “for my sake”) for emphasis.
The Hebrew text reads literally, “for how can it be defiled?” The subject of the verb is probably “name” (v. 9).

verses.zh: 雅各―我所选召的以色列啊，当听我言：我是耶和华，我是首先的，也是末后的。
verses.en: Listen to me, O Jacob,Israel, whom I summoned.I am the one;I am present at the very beginningand at the very end.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “I [am] he, I [am the] first, also I [am the] last.”

verses.zh: 我手立了地的根基；我右手铺张诸天；我一招呼便都立住。
verses.en: Yes, my hand founded the earth;my right hand spread out the sky.I summon them;they stand together.

verses.zh: 你们都当聚集而听，他们（或译：偶像）内中谁说过这些事？耶和华所爱的人必向巴比伦行他所喜悦的事；他的膀臂也要加在迦勒底人身上。
verses.en: All of you, gather together and listen!Who among them[NOTE:1] announced these things?The Lord’s ally[NOTE:2] will carry out his desire against Babylon;he will exert his power against the Babylonians.[NOTE:3]
notes: This probably refers to the idol gods (see v. 5).
The Lord’s ally is a reference to Cyrus.tn Or “friend,” or “covenant partner.”
Heb “and his arm [against] the Babylonians.”

verses.zh: 惟有我曾说过，我又选召他，领他来，他的道路就必亨通。
verses.en: I, I have spoken—yes, I have summoned him;I lead him and he will succeed.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and his way will be prosperous.”

verses.zh: 你们要就近我来听这话：我从起头并未曾在隐密处说话；自从有这事，我就在那里。现在，主耶和华差遣我和他的灵来（或译：耶和华和他的灵差遣我来）。
verses.en: Approach me—listen to this!From the very first I have not spoken in secret;when it happens,[NOTE:1] I am there.”So now, the Sovereign Lord has sent me, accompanied by his Spirit.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “from the time of its occurring.”
The speaker here is not identified specifically, but he is probably Cyrus, the Lord’s “ally” mentioned in vv. 14-15.

verses.zh: 耶和华―你的救赎主，以色列的圣者如此说：我是耶和华―你的　神，教训你，使你得益处，引导你所当行的路。
verses.en: This is what the Lord, your Protector,[NOTE:1] says,the Holy One of Israel:[NOTE:2] “I am the Lord your God,who teaches you how to succeed,who leads you in the way you should go.
notes: Heb “your redeemer.” See the note at 41:14.
See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

verses.zh: 甚愿你素来听从我的命令！你的平安就如河水；你的公义就如海浪。
verses.en: If only you had obeyed my[NOTE:1] commandments,prosperity would have flowed to you like a river,[NOTE:2] deliverance would have come to you like the waves of the sea.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “paid attention to” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV); TEV “had listened to.”
Heb “like a river your peace would have been.” שָׁלוֹם (shalom) probably refers here to the peace and prosperity which God promised in return for obedience to the covenant.
Heb “and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.” צְדָקָה (tsedaqah) probably refers here to divine deliverance from enemies. See v. 19.

verses.zh: 你的后裔也必多如海沙；你腹中所生的也必多如沙粒。他的名在我面前必不剪除，也不灭绝。
verses.en: Your descendants would have been as numerous as sand[NOTE:1] and your children[NOTE:2] like its granules.Their name would not have been cut offand eliminated from my presence.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “like sand”; NCV “as many as the grains of sand.”
Heb “and the issue from your inner parts.”
Heb “and his name would not be cut off and would not be destroyed from before me.”

verses.zh: 你们要从巴比伦出来，从迦勒底人中逃脱，以欢呼的声音传扬说：耶和华救赎了他的仆人雅各！你们要将这事宣扬到地极。
verses.en: Leave Babylon!Flee from the Babylonians!Announce it with a shout of joy!Make this known—proclaim it throughout the earth![NOTE:1] Say, ‘The Lord protects[NOTE:2] his servant Jacob.
notes: Heb “to the end of the earth” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV).
Heb “redeems.” See the note at 41:14.

verses.zh: 耶和华引导他们经过沙漠。他们并不干渴；他为他们使水从磐石而流，分裂磐石，水就涌出。
verses.en: They do not thirst as he leads them through dry regions;he makes water flow out of a rock for them;he splits open a rock and water flows out.’[NOTE:1]
notes: The translation above (present tense) assumes that this verse describes God’s provision for returning Babylonian exiles (see v. 20; 35:6; 49:10) in terms reminiscent of the Exodus from Egypt (see Exod 17:6).

verses.zh: 耶和华说：恶人必不得平安！
verses.en: There will be no prosperity for the wicked,” says the Lord.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- As YHWH addressed Neo-Babylon in Isaiah 46 and 47, He now addresses His people, His returnees,
His faithful remnant.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (three senses)

- Notice the different ways Israel is referred to.

- O house of Jacob, Isa. 48:1

- who are named Israel, Isa. 48:1

- who came from the loins of Judah, Isa. 48:1

- who swear by the name of the Lord, Isa. 48:1

- who invoke the God of Israel, Isa. 48:1

- you are obstinate, Isa. 48:4

- you have been called a rebel from birth, Isa. 48:8

- O Jacob, Isa. 48:12,20

- Notice the different titles and descriptions of YHWH

- the name of the Lord, Isa. 48:1

- the God of Israel, Isa. 48:1,2

- I am He, Isa. 48:12

- I am the first, I am the last, Isa. 48:12

- the Lord (YHWH), Isa. 48:14,17,20,22

- the Lord God (Adon YHWH), Isa. 48:16

- Redeemer, Isa. 48:17

- the Holy One, Isa. 48:17

- the Lord your God, Isa. 48:17

- There are several significant and theologically important verses in this section of Isaiah that
will be developed in the NT.

- Isa. 45:23

- Isa. 46:8-11

- Isa. 48:8-11

- Isa. 48:16

- H. C. Leupold entitles this chapter "A Sharp Rebuke and a Gracious Challenge" (p. 158). This
fluctuation between judgment and mercy characterizes prophetic literature and it happens side
by side with little or no textual transition markers.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 48:1-11

1"Hear this, O house of Jacob, who are named Israel

And who came forth from the loins of Judah,

Who swear by the name of the Lord

And invoke the God of Israel,

But not in truth nor in righteousness.

2For they call themselves after the holy city

And lean on the God of Israel;

The Lord of hosts is His name.

3I declared the former things long ago

And they went forth from My mouth, and I proclaimed them.

Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.

4Because I know that you are obstinate,

And your neck is an iron sinew

And your forehead bronze,

5Therefore I declared them to you long ago,

Before they took place I proclaimed them to you,

So that you would not say, 'My idol has done them,

And my graven image and my molten image have commanded them.'

6You have heard; look at all this.

And you, will you not declare it?

I proclaim to you new things from this time,

Even hidden things which you have not known.

7They are created now and not long ago;

And before today you have not heard them,

So that you will not say, 'Behold, I knew them.'

8You have not heard, you have not known.

Even from long ago your ear has not been open,

Because I knew that you would deal very treacherously;

And you have been called a rebel from birth.

9For the sake of My name I delay My wrath,

And for My praise I restrain it for you,

In order not to cut you off.

10Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver;

I have tested you in the furnace of affliction.

11For My own sake, for My own sake, I will act;

For how can My name be profaned?

And My glory I will not give to another."

48:1 "Hear" This is a common IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033, KB 1570) for Isaiah,
as well as Deuteronomy, Kings, Job, Psalm, and Amos, to begin a new section (cf. Isa. 1:2,10; 7:13;
28:23; 36:13; 37:17; 47:8; 46:3,12; 47:8; 48:1,14,16; 49:1; 51:1,7; 55:2; 66:5). YHWH wants His message
"heard" and "lived out." Divine revelation demands obedience! Truth is not only mental but lifestyle!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ "Israel" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

▣

NASB, NRSV, Peshitta
"from the loins of Judah"

NKJV
"from the wellsprings of Judah"

TEV
"you who are descended from Judah"

NJB
"issued from the waters of Judah"

REB
"from the seed of Judah"

LXX
"came forth out of Judah"

JPSOA
"have issued from the waters of Judah"

There are three Hebrew roots used by commentators to attempt to explain this text.

- "waters," מי (BDB 565, the UBS Text Project, p. 128, gives the MT a "B" rating)

- "loins," מעי (BDB 588, NASB, NRSV, AB; DSS, "from the inward parts")

- "seed," זרע (BDB 281, REB)

All of these Hebrew terms are imagery for the descendants by natural means
of a group, tribe, family. The UBS Text Project, p. 128, gives "from the waters" a B rating.

Notice that all the descendants are designated by

- Jacob

- Israel

- Judah

This implies the returnees were mostly from the southern three tribes called Judah. "Israel" now
refers to all of Abraham's seed, as it did before the United Monarchy split in 922 B.C.

▣ "Who swear. . .invoke" Both of these VERBS refer to worship acts.

- swear by the name (BDB 989, KB 1396, Niphal PARTICIPLE, cf. Isa. 19:18; 65:16)

- invoke (lit. "cause to remember," BDB 269, KB 269, Hiphil IMPERFECT, cf. Isa. 12:4; 26:13; 62:6)

▣

NASB. NKJV, LXX
"But not in truth nor in righteousness"

NRSV
"But not in truth or right"

TEV
"But you don't mean a word you say"

NJB
"Though not in good faith or uprightness"

JPSOA
"Though not in truth and sincerity"

REB
"But not with honesty and sincerity"

Wow, what a condemning evaluation of Israel's worship!

- The term "truth" is אמת (BDB 54) and means "faithfulness." See

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT

- For the second word, צדקה (BDB 842) see

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

48:2 The first two lines remind me of Jeremiah's "Temple Sermon" in Jeremiah 7, where
the Israelites trust in the temple but not in YHWH.

- call themselves after the holy city (BDB 894, KB 1128, Niphal PERFECT, cf. Isa. 48:1)

- lean on the God of Israel (BDB 701, KB 759, Niphal PERFECT)

Their worship looked orthodox and pious but it was false and directed to the wrong source.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

48:3 YHWH again speaks (notice the number of "I's") of His control of time and history. He uses
predictive prophecy to show His people His existence and power (v. 5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

48:4 YHWH describes His people as

- obstinate (cf. Ezek. 2:4; 3:7)

- neck is an iron sinew

- forehead is bronze

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS

▣ "know" This word (BDB 393, KB 390) is used several times in this chapter
(cf. Isa. 48:4,6,7,8 [twice]), where it means "knowledge about," but it should mean "intimate
fellowship with."

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

48:5 "idol" This verse mentions two kinds of false images of deities (cf. Isa. 40:20; 46:5-7).

- carved from wood (cf. Isa. 44:9-17; Jer. 10:1-10)

- cast of metal in a mold (cf. Isa. 30:22; 40:19; 41:7)

48:6 There is some question about how the VERBS of the first two lines
should be translated. I like the NJB's version, "You have heard and seen all this, why won't you admit it?"

The "it" refers to YHWH's predictions (cf. Isa. 42:9; 43:19; 48:5). YHWH proves His existence by
His knowledge of and control of future events affecting all nations not just Israel/Judah.

For "new things" see full note at Isa. 62:2.

48:8 "deal very treacherously" This intensified grammatical form is a Qal IMPERFECT
and a Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of the same root (BDB 93, KB 108). A good example is Jer. 44:15-19.

▣ "a rebel from birth" See Deut. 9:7. Even in the exit from Egypt, Israel was idolatrous
(i.e. Ezek. 20:8,13; Amos 5:25-26).

48:9 This is a good summary of YHWH's problem with Abraham's seed. He wanted to use
them so that the world would know Him and come to Him (cf. Gen. 12:3). But they were not faithful. He
had declared, "the soul that sins it will die" (i.e. Gen. 2:16,17; Ezek. 18:4,20). Now God's word and God's
purpose come into conflict. He will choose to act for the greater good (i.e. salvation of all humans,
cf. 1 Sam. 12:22; Ps. 106:8; Jer. 14:7; Ezek. 20:8-9,14,17). The text that describes this so well is
Ezek. 36:22-36! YHWH acts for Israel for His greater purpose! Is this not what Isa. 48:11 is affirming?
This is the wonderful message of Isaiah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

48:10

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA
"tested"

NRSV, Peshitta
"refined"

NJB
"chosen"

REB
"purified"

LXX
"delivered"

The MT has the VERB "choose" (בחר,
BDB 103, KB 119, Qal PERFECT, NJB), but the DSS scroll of Isaiah has a similar
VERB "tested" (בחן, BDB 103, KB 119), which fits the context better.
The UBS Text Project gives "refined" a "B" rating.

48:11 This verse is similar in content to Ezek. 36:22-36. The last line is reflected in Isa. 42:8.

▣

NASB
"how can My name be profaned?"

NKJV
"how should My name be profaned?""

NRSV, NJB
"why should My name be profaned?"

TEV
"I will not let my name be dishonored"

REB
"I will not let my name be profaned"

JPSOA
"Lest [My name} be dishonored!"

Peshitta
"that my name may not be polluted"

LXX
"because my name is profaned"

In the UBS Text Project, p. 130, the committee gives four possible textual
options, but it cannot decide which one is original.

- how should it be profaned

- how should my name be profaned

- how should I be profaned

- how should my praise be profaned

It chose option 3 as the best guess.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 48:12-16

12"Listen to Me, O Jacob, even Israel whom I called;

I am He, I am the first, I am also the last.

13Surely My hand founded the earth,

And My right hand spread out the heavens;

When I call to them, they stand together.

14Assemble, all of you, and listen!

Who among them has declared these things?

The Lord loves him; he will carry out His good pleasure on Babylon,

And His arm will be against the Chaldeans.

15I, even I, have spoken; indeed I have called him,

I have brought him, and He will make his ways successful.

16Come near to Me, listen to this:

From the first I have not spoken in secret,

From the time it took place, I was there.

And now the Lord God has sent Me, and His Spirit."

48:12 "Listen" See full note at v. 1.

▣ "I am He, I am the first, I am also the last" This is a recurrent idiom in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 41:4; 44:6)
and becomes a common designation for Christ in Rev. 1:17; 2:8; 22:13! It is theologically parallel to "I am the
Alpha and Omega" (cf. Rev. 1:8). It denotes the God of creation (Isa. 48:13; Jesus was the Father's agent in creation,
cf. John 1:3,10; 1 Cor. 8:6; Col. 1:16; Heb. 1:2) and eternity—eternity past, eternity future (i.e. time). The only God is YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

48:14 "Assemble, all of you" This command to gather (BDB 867, KB 1062, Niphal
IMPERATIVE) refers to "O Jacob, even Israel" of v. 12.

▣ "listen" See note at 48:1.

▣ "Who among them has declared these things" The "who" seems, in context, to refer to the
astrologers, false propehts, and enchanters of Isa. 42:11. YHWH shows His reality by His predictions and
actions, which surprised the hearers.
